title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 10th Congressional District
area: South-central Pennsylvania, including Cumberland and Dauphin (Harrisburg) counties and part of York County.

context.text: Ballotpedia identified this race as a battleground, and as of July 2026 major election forecasters rated it a Toss-up. Scott Perry won re-election 53.8%-46.2% in 2022 and defeated Janelle Stelson 50.5%-49.3% in 2024, when Donald Trump (R) carried the district 52.0%-46.8% over Kamala Harris. As of June 30, 2026, Perry had raised $5.19 million and Stelson had raised $6.36 million.

PoliticsPA's Louis Jacobson wrote that Perry was the most vulnerable House Republican incumbent on the 2026 ballot: "he has articulated the most conservative views of the four vulnerable Republicans on our list despite representing a district that went to Donald Trump in 2024 by a modest five points ... Republicans paint Perry as a survivor."

Janelle Stelson defeated Justin Douglas in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary; Scott Perry was unopposed in the Republican primary. Isabelle Harman (Independent) did not make the general-election ballot, according to Ballotpedia.

summary.text: Scott Perry is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 10th District, first elected in 2012. He is a Pennsylvania Army National Guard veteran who reached the rank of Assistant Adjutant General (his campaign describes him as a Brigadier General) and previously worked as the owner of a mechanical contracting business. For the 2025-2026 Congress he serves on the House Committees on Oversight and Government Reform and Transportation and Infrastructure, and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.

background.text: Born in San Diego, California, in 1962; earned a B.S. in business administration management from Pennsylvania State University in 1991.

Served in the Pennsylvania Army National Guard from 1980 to 2019, reaching the rank of Assistant Adjutant General; campaign materials describe him as reaching the rank of Brigadier General and commanding units in Iraq.
Served in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives from 2007 to 2012, and was previously chairman of the Carroll Township Planning Commission.
Worked as the owner of a mechanical contracting business and as an insurance agent before his political career.

priorities.text: Campaign describes him as bringing "a diverse background in business, military, and community service" to Congress, citing nearly 40 years in the military and his work commanding units in Iraq.
priorities.quote: He started working at 13 and co-founded a mechanical contracting firm. With nearly 40 years in the military, he achieved the rank of Brigadier General, commanding units in Iraq and earning a Master's in Strategic Studies from the U.S. Army War College.

positions.summary: Supports securing the border, deporting violent criminals and drug dealers, banning sanctuary cities, and providing Border Patrol agents more resources.
positions.quote: He supports: Securing our borders; Deporting violent criminals, drug dealers and terrorists; Banning sanctuary cities; Providing Border Patrol agents with the resources to do their jobs.

positions.summary: Opposes tax increases on small businesses and families, and supports a Balanced Budget Amendment and less government regulation.
positions.quote: Scott opposes Biden-Harris' tax-and-spend increases on small businesses and working families. He'll continue to fight for: A Balanced Budget Amendment; Less government regulation.

positions.summary: Supports a "blended energy portfolio" centered on natural gas, hydroelectric, and nuclear power to reduce dependence on foreign energy, rather than a faster transition away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: Pennsylvania plays a critical role in returning America to energy independence by supporting our vast natural gas reserves and harnessing hydroelectric and nuclear power.

positions.summary: Opposes "Medicare for All" and single-payer health care and extending Social Security or Medicare benefits to non-U.S. citizens. Opponent Janelle Stelson's campaign says he "was the deciding vote on a bill that would cut health care for nearly 20,000 people in our area" and quotes him calling a reduction in health-insurance costs a "colossal mistake."
positions.quote: He is opposed to the socialist "Medicare for All" and single-payer healthcare, and any attempt to provide illegals and non-U.S. citizens with Social Security and/or Medicare benefits.

record.text: Assigned to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (chairing the Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee), and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.name: Janelle Stelson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary, defeating Justin Douglas

summary.text: Janelle Stelson is a former WGAL-TV news anchor and reporter who covered central Pennsylvania for 26 years. She narrowly lost to incumbent Scott Perry in 2024 (50.5%-49.3%) and is running again in 2026, campaigning on lowering the cost of living, health care, and congressional ethics reform.

background.text: Born in Fairbanks, Alaska, and grew up in the Seattle area of Washington; earned a B.A. in politics and government from the University of Puget Sound.
Worked for 26 years as a news anchor, reporter, and weather anchor at WGAL-TV in central Pennsylvania. Her first job was writing speeches for the Egyptian embassy in Washington, D.C.

priorities.text: Says Central Pennsylvanians are being squeezed by rising costs while Perry "supports the chaotic policy of ever-changing tariff-taxes that raise prices and kill jobs" and was "the deciding vote on a budget that slashes food assistance, raises utility bills and adds $3.4 trillion dollars in new debt."
priorities.quote: Central Pennsylvanians are working harder than ever and falling further behind. We are being squeezed by the rising cost of everything from groceries to health care.

priorities.text: Proposes a congressional ethics plan including 12-year term limits for herself, a ban on members of Congress trading individual stocks, a lifetime lobbying ban for former members, and a stronger, independent Congressional Ethics Agency.
priorities.quote: Limit terms to 12 years. Even if Congress does not act to require term limits, I will limit my own terms and will not serve more than 12 years.

priorities.text: Says she supports high-quality, affordable health care with better access to urgent and primary care, and opposes surprise medical billing.

positions.summary: Opposes broad tariffs, saying she would repeal what she calls Perry's "tariff taxes" that are increasing costs.
positions.quote: I will repeal these tariff taxes that are increasing costs and vote to end the war in Iran.

positions.summary: Supports tax breaks for the "hard-working middle class, not billionaires," and opposes continuing tax breaks for the wealthy and a proposed new national sales tax.
positions.quote: I support tax breaks for the hard-working middle class, not billionaires.

positions.summary: Supports cutting red tape to make it faster and cheaper to build homes, expanding small-dollar home loans, and rewarding towns that build more housing.
positions.quote: Cut Red Tape to Make it Faster and Easier to Build Homes; Make Homes Cheaper to Build; Expand Small-dollar Home Loans; Reward Towns that Actually Build More Homes.

positions.summary: Supports allowing the government to negotiate prescription-drug prices, banning surprise medical billing, and removing medical debt from credit reports.
positions.quote: I support lowering the price of prescription drugs by allowing the government to negotiate prices... I believe medical debt should be taken off credit reports.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; ran unsuccessfully for this seat in 2024.
